score_notes.scripture: Disciples of Christ broadly accepts historical-critical scholarship; non-inerrantist.

score_notes.leadership: Congregationalist Restorationist polity; senior minister + board.
score_notes.soteriology: DoC heritage affirms believer's baptism by immersion for remission of sins — Stone-Campbell sacramental framework; mainline drift on doctrinal specifics.
score_notes.cultural: DoC is Open & Affirming friendly; NCCC publicly progressive on LGBT inclusion; per MOOP rubric = red.
score_notes.preaching: Topical, lectionary-based mainline preaching; progressive social-gospel orientation.
score_notes.mission: DoC Week of Compassion (denominational humanitarian fund); Wider Mission.
score_notes.denominational: Disciples of Christ has been on a progressive mainline trajectory for decades; ordained gay clergy and many congregations are Open & Affirming. Per rubric = red.

churches.assessment: National City Christian Church is the architectural and ecclesiastical "cathedral" of the Christian Church (Disciples of Christ) — a neoclassical John Russell Pope landmark on Thomas Circle, completed 1930, with stained-glass windows commemorating Presidents James A. Garfield and Lyndon B. Johnson, both Disciples. President Johnson occasionally attended during his presidency and his state funeral was held here on January 25, 1973. The church called The Rev. Stephanie Kendell as its first female senior pastor and president in 2023 — she previously served as 1st Vice-Moderator of the entire denomination. Disciples of Christ as a whole is mainline-progressive: non-inerrantist, egalitarian, with many Open & Affirming congregations and openly affirming LGBT clergy. NCCC publicly aligns with this trajectory. By MOOP's rubric the church is red across gender, cultural, denominational, and preaching dimensions — beautiful building, beautiful presidential history, theological distance significant.
